segments.description: Coaches, our next presenter is Steve Blundell, a tennis Australia high-performance coach who has over 20 years of experience in mentoring players across all levels. Knowing for his holistic approach to player development, Steve has led Australian teams both nationally and internationally. In his session today around the importance of having a mentor, Steve will take a deep dive into some of the ways that you as coaches can link with a mentor and then the benefits you will reap by doing so. Please welcome Steve. Thank you to Tennis Australia for having me on the conference this year. Always a great honour. The power of mentors is something I'd like to touch on today with the time we have. As people we always have a fascination with success and the stories that surround success. We well know that success often leaves clues. However, we also know that in an ever-changing environment, while some secrets to success will never change throughout the generations, there are some that will evolve and interact. Having a mentor has been quite the buzzword for some time. Highlighted to me two or three weeks ago when my little 10-year-old Super Tens player asked me if I would be his mentor. When I asked him what mentor meant to him, he said, I really don't know. I just know it's really important to have one, which made me chuckle and realise just how important this topic is.
